incidents.cause: The pilot’s inadequate in-flight fuel planning, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
The pilot's selection of unsuitable terrain for landing, which resulted in structural damage to the airplane during landing.
Fatigue failure of the nose wheel fork, which resulted in separation of the nose wheel.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain directional control, and the flight instructor’s delayed remedial action.
The pilot's loss of control while landing in gusting wind conditions.
The loss of engine power after departure due to the separation of an engine cylinder.

The pilot’s failure to execute a missed approach after recognizing that the airplane was not aligned with the wet runway, which resulted in a long landing with a tailwind and a subsequent runway overrun.
The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing. Contributing to the accident was an inoperative landing gear warning horn.
The student pilot’s loss of directional control during the landing roll and his subsequent inadvertent brake application, which resulted in a nose-over.
The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with taxiway signage.
